topic: Why you're always tired even after 8 hours of sleep
title: Why 8 Hours Of Sleep Still Leaves You Tired
hook_promise: Why you can sleep eight hours and still wake up exhausted: broken sleep, a slow brain reboot, and a body that never switched off.

beats.narration: Eight hours in bed. Still exhausted?
beats.visual_intent: The lead sits slumped on the edge of a rumpled bed in golden morning light, hand on forehead, while the tidy alarm clock beside the bed shows the night is over.

shot.image_prompt: Cozy bedroom in warm golden morning sun with dappled window shadows. The lead sits slumped on the edge of a rumpled bed with a quilt tumbled behind. One mitten hand rests on the forehead, eyes heavy and tired. A small round alarm clock and a green coffee cup sit on a wooden nightstand.
pose_variants: The lead slumps further forward with both hands covering the face, shoulders drooping.
The lead sits upright with eyes wide open in weary disbelief, one hand lifted palm up.

beats.narration: Sleep isn't just time. Quality can break without you ever waking up.
beats.visual_intent: Top-down view of the lead asleep under a patchwork quilt full of small torn holes, with beams of light poking through, a metaphor for sleep that is fragmented but unnoticed.

shot.image_prompt: Top-down view of the lead lying peacefully asleep in a wooden bed under a patchwork quilt. The quilt has several small ragged holes with soft golden light streaming through them onto the sheets. Warm cozy bedroom light, a pillow under the white round head, eyes closed and calm.

beats.narration: Your airway muscles relax and block airflow. Your brain jolts you half-awake, again and again.
beats.visual_intent: Close-up of the sleeping lead with a soft ribbon of pale air pinched shut in a kinked line near the face, then the eyes pop half-open for a moment.

shot.image_prompt: Close-up of the lead's large white round head on a pillow in a dim warm bedroom lit by a soft lamp glow. Eyes gently closed. A ribbon of pale blue air wisps near the face is pinched and kinked like a bent garden hose, no letters or numbers anywhere.
pose_variants: The lead's eyes snap half-open, brows lifted in a startled, groggy look, head slightly raised from the pillow.

beats.narration: That's sleep apnea. Tens of millions of Americans have it.
beats.visual_intent: Wide shot through the café window of a sunlit street full of yawning, trudging round-headed figures, the lead and friend watching from inside; a quiet health note lands at the end.

shot.image_prompt: Warm sunlit café interior with a wooden round table and green coffee cups. The lead and the friend in the teal scarf sit at the window looking out. Through the tall window a busy golden street is full of many small white round-headed figures, some yawning, some slumped, walking sleepily. Ivy and plants frame the window.

beats.narration: But maybe your night was fine. Then the trouble starts at the alarm.
beats.visual_intent: A jump to morning: an arm reaches out from under the quilt toward a ringing alarm clock on the nightstand.

shot.image_prompt: Bedroom in bright early morning sun with long shadows. The lead is half under a tumbled quilt, one slim navy arm stretched out with a mitten hand toward a small round alarm clock on a wooden nightstand, face squinting and reluctant. Green plant on the windowsill.

beats.narration: That's sleep inertia. Parts of your brain wake up slower than others, so you start the day groggy.
beats.visual_intent: The lead sits on the bed edge, heavy-lidded; above the head hangs a row of small lamps, some glowing and some dark, to show parts of the brain waking at different speeds.

shot.image_prompt: Cozy bedroom in golden morning light: the lead sits on the edge of the bed with heavy-lidded eyes and a hand on the forehead, swaying slightly, the patchwork quilt rumpled behind, the nightstand with the alarm clock beside the bed; above the lead's head hangs a row of small lamps on cords, some glowing warm and some dark, dappled shadows on the wall.
pose_variants: The lead's head tilts heavily to one side, eyes nearly closed, both hands hanging limp.

motion.detail: a row of small lamps, some lit and some dark

beats.narration: And stress? It keeps your nervous system alert, even while you sleep.
beats.visual_intent: The lead lies in bed at night with eyes wide open, a tight tangled knot of red thread floating above like a worry that won't loosen.

shot.image_prompt: Dim bedroom at night with a soft warm lamp glow. The lead lies on the back in bed, quilt pulled to the chest, eyes wide open staring upward. A tight tangled knot of red thread floats above the face. Moonlight through the window.
pose_variants: The lead turns to one side, eyes still wide open and brows tense, mitten hands gripping the quilt.

beats.narration: So eight hours can still be broken sleep, a slow brain reboot, or a body that never powered down.
beats.visual_intent: Top-down of the café table with three painted objects, a torn quilt scrap, a dim lamp and a tight coiled spring, each ticked off one by one as the three reasons.

shot.image_prompt: Top-down view of a round wooden café table in warm golden light. Three objects are laid out in a row: a torn scrap of patchwork quilt, a small dim lamp, and a tightly wound metal spring. A green coffee cup sits at the edge of the table.

motion.detail: Broken sleep | Slow brain reboot | Never powered down

beats.narration: Next time you're wiped out, ask: was that eight hours, or eight good ones?
beats.visual_intent: The lead and friend sit at the café table with two green cups side by side, one full and steaming and one drained, to contrast quantity with quality.

shot.image_prompt: Sunlit café, round wooden table. The lead and the friend in the teal scarf sit facing each other. Two green cups sit side by side on the table, one brimming and steaming, one nearly empty. The friend leans in with a thoughtful tilt of the head, the lead smiles gently. Hanging lamp, ivy, tall windows with a golden street.
pose_variants: The lead lifts their full cup slightly toward the friend with a small smile; the friend nods, hands around the drained cup.

sources.claim: conditions such as sleep apnea, snoring, restless movements, or frequent micro-awakenings can fragment sleep without fully waking you up.
sources.title: Still Tired After 8 Hours of Sleep? What It Could Mean for Your Health
sources.quote: Conditions such as sleep apnea, snoring, restless movements, or frequent micro-awakenings can fragment sleep without fully waking you up.

sources.claim: muscles in your airway relax and either partially or completely block airflow, and the sleeper often doesn't remember the repeated brief awakenings that follow.
sources.title: How Common Is Sleep Apnea? Prevalence and Who's Most at Risk
sources.quote: Obstructive sleep apnea happens when muscles in your airway relax and either partially or completely block airflow.

sources.claim: 80 to 83 million people in the United States are estimated to have obstructive sleep apnea, according to the American Sleep Apnea Association.
sources.title: How Common Is Sleep Apnea? Prevalence and Who's Most at Risk
sources.quote:
## Prevalence of Sleep Apnea
In the United States, about 80 to 83 million people are estimated to have obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) — the most common...

sources.claim: after a long sleep episode of 7 to 8 hours, people tend to feel groggy from sleep inertia, a temporary decline in performance and mood after waking.
sources.title: Module 7. Napping, an Important Fatigue Countermeasure, Sleep Inertia
sources.quote: After awakening from a nap or a long sleep episode (for example, 7 to 8 hours of sleep at night), people tend to feel groggy from sleep inertia.

sources.claim: ongoing mental or emotional stress keeps the nervous system activated, signaling your body to remain alert even during sleep.
sources.title: Still Tired After 8 Hours of Sleep? What It Could Mean for Your Health
sources.quote: Ongoing mental or emotional stress keeps the nervous system activated, signaling your body to remain alert even during sleep.

sources.claim: obstructive sleep apnea affects an estimated 29.4 million US adults, about 12 percent of the adult population, with roughly 80 percent undiagnosed (a 2016 Frost & Sullivan analysis commissioned by the American Academy of Sleep Medicine).
sources.title: Hidden health crisis costing America billions (AASM / Frost & Sullivan, 2016)
sources.quote: user-supplied figure (AASM ~29.4M); URL found by web search, not by the research call

pipeline: all three have the legs out of bed with feet on the floor; the brief says lying on the back under the quilt

direction.lead-bed-awake-bedroom: now LYING FLAT ON THEIR BACK IN THE BED AT NIGHT: the whole body is stretched out along the mattress and hidden under the patchwork quilt of rust, cream and teal squares from the chest down to the feet, so no legs and no feet are visible and nothing hangs over the side of the bed. Seen from beside the bed and slightly above, the bed runs down the frame with the wooden headboard and the pale pillow at the top and the foot of the bed at the bottom. The round white head rests on the pillow, face turned up toward the ceiling with both eyes open and two small eyebrows, a calm natural face. Both navy mitten hands rest on top of the quilt over the chest. The small wooden nightstand from the first image stands right beside the pillow within arm's reach, with ONE round alarm clock standing upright and level in the middle of its top, and the brass lamp switched on, glowing warm. Behind, a window with cool blue moonlight and a plain night sky, nothing in the window but sky. Warm lamp light on the quilt, cool moonlight from the window, cozy
